title: Who can apply (ukri.org)
text:
This funding opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility. Check if your organisation is eligible .
This funding opportunity is open to:
PhD students currently funded by AHRC
early career researchers (ECRs) in any arts or humanities subject
You must apply to undertake primary research in an AHRC subject area for all hosts.
You can apply for a placement at more than one institution in a single round, noting that separate applications need to be submitted. However:
applications must be for separate and distinct research work packages
dates must not overlap
total placement length cannot be longer than the maximum total length of five months
placements must take place in one continuous block of time
applications must not be interdependent
you should stay in-country for the duration of the placement
You can only hold a placement at the same institution once in each stage of your career, for example once as a PhD student and once as an ECR.
Deferred entry applications are not permitted except under exceptional circumstances, where you should contact us at the earliest opportunity. Equally, if your application is successful but you cannot undertake your placement, you must reapply the following year.
Before applying, PhD students must secure approval of their UK research organisation and their supervisor. ECRs must secure approval from their head of department. This approval confirms that you can attend the placement in full if your application is successful.
Who is eligible to apply
Individual eligibility for PhD students
You must be a doctoral student currently funded by AHRC to be eligible to apply to any host.
Placements must be undertaken during the funded period of your doctoral award.
PhD students must include their doctoral training grant reference in the ‘About you’ section of the application form.
Because these placements are intended to enrich and form part of the period of doctoral study, no additional time will be added to the doctoral award end date.
Individual eligibility for ECRs
Anyone who considers their role to be that of an ECR may self-identity as one. There are no eligibility rules based on how many years have passed since the award of your PhD.
You must be employed and supported by an eligible UK research organisation with a contract that extends for at least the duration of your grant under the International Placement Scheme. You will need to demonstrate that a contract is in place at the point of application submission. However, it is not a requirement to have a permanent employment contract to apply for funding.
If you are identifying as an ECR, you must either:
hold a doctorate by the start date of the research grant
demonstrate equivalent research or innovation experience, training, or both
To support you in determining whether you could identify as an ECR, you are encouraged to consider whether you meet at least one of the criteria of career stage and research trajectory below. You have:
not previously held a major role as a project lead or co lead on a funded academic research project funded by AHRC, UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) or any other funder
not previously led or co led a substantial research programme in a commercial or non academic setting
recently returned from a career break (for example, parental leave, caring responsibilities, sickness, or an unpaid sabbatical)
recently experienced a significant career transition, such as moving from industry to academia, or returning to a permanent academic role after holding substantial administrative responsibilities
Where previous AHRC or UKRI funding has been held, ECRs must include their previous grant reference in the application form.
See further guidance on career and skills development for early career researchers .
Resubmissions
We will not accept uninvited resubmissions of projects that have been submitted to UKRI. Find out more about UKRI’s resubmission policy .
Equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI)
We are committed to achieving equality of opportunity for all funding applicants. We encourage applications from a diverse range of researchers.
We support people to work in a way that suits their personal circumstances. This includes:
career breaks
support for people with caring responsibilities
flexible working
alternative working patterns
We are committed to promoting the values of equality of opportunity, diversity, and inclusivity. A dynamic, diverse and inclusive research and innovation system must be an integral part of UK society, giving everyone the opportunity to participate and to benefit. Therefore, we particularly encourage applications from persons who identify as:
an ethnic minority
people with health conditions or impairments
people with caring responsibilities
persons of diverse gender identities and expressions
persons identifying with other groups who are currently underrepresented
Applicants who identify with any of the protected characteristics listed above and who would welcome additional support, or who wish to discuss any perceived risks or concerns, are encouraged to contact us and their prospective host institutions for further guidance and support.
UKRI can offer disability and accessibility support for UKRI applicants and grant holders during the application and assessment process.
Applicants with disabilities or caring responsibilities may request an appropriate amount of additional funding where this is essential to taking up the placement and where it cannot be provided by routes such as the UKRI disabled students allowance . Applicants requiring this additional support should contact AHRC for further guidance and to discuss how to reflect this request within the application form.
Applications to UKRI through the new UKRI Funding Service can only be made if you have completed our EDI survey, which you are prompted to do when you open a Funding Service account. However, diversity information will never be used in the assessment process nor to make funding decisions.
